items.title: FEU and La Salle secure UAAP women’s table tennis semifinal spots
items.summary: FEU and La Salle claimed the first two UAAP Season 89 women’s table tennis Final Four places in Mandaluyong. Mikylla Dinauano helped FEU beat Ateneo 3–1 and UST 3–0, while Angel Laude led La Salle’s 3–0 sweeps of UE and Adamson.
items.image_alt: FEU’s Mikylla Dinauano competing in UAAP Season 89 table tennis
items.image_credit: UAAP Season 89 Media Team / Tiebreaker Times

items.title: La Salle and Letran claim narrow PGFlex Invitational wins
items.summary: La Salle beat Olivarez 78–76 as Agjanti Miller scored 30 points and grabbed 12 rebounds in the PGFlex Invitational Quintana Cup. Letran edged Manila Central University 78–77 to move to 2–0 and take the solo lead, with Aaron Levy contributing 19 points.
items.image_alt: La Salle’s Guillian Quines in PGFlex Invitational action against Olivarez

items.title: UST reaches UAAP table tennis Final Four with 64th straight win
items.summary: UST secured the first UAAP Season 89 men’s table tennis Final Four berth after beating Adamson 3–0 and Ateneo 3–1. Eljay Tormis clinched the victory over Ateneo, extending the defending champions’ winning streak to 64 matches at Gameville Central Park in Mandaluyong.
items.image_alt: UST’s Jebb Datahan competing in UAAP Season 89 table tennis
items.image_credit: UAAP Season 89 Media Team / Tiebreaker Times

items.title: Farm Fresh wins five-set battle with PLDT to take solo third
items.summary: Farm Fresh defeated PLDT 20–25, 25–17, 23–25, 25–20, 17–15 to take solo third in the PVL Siklab Series. The Foxies improved to 4–2 and ended PLDT’s three-match winning streak at Smart Araneta Coliseum on November 10.
items.image_alt: Farm Fresh’s Trisha Tubu in PVL action against PLDT

items.title: Villados earns Spikers’ Turf weekly award for Criss Cross
items.summary: Criss Cross setter Adrian Villados earned Spikers’ Turf Press Corps Player of the Week honours for November 3–8. He delivered 38 excellent sets against NU-Archipelago Builders and 18 against AEP-Cabstars, helping the King Crunchers remain unbeaten through five Invitational Conference matches.

items.title: Nouri earns International Master title with ASEAN+ bronze
items.summary: Alekhine Nouri earned the International Master title after finishing third at the ASEAN+ Individual Chess Championships in Misamis Occidental. The 20-year-old FEU player beat Michael Concio Jr. in the final round, reaching six points and taking bronze through the best tiebreak score.
items.image_alt: Alekhine Nouri featured in the report on his International Master title

items.title: Carlos Yulo returns to French gymnastics club for another season
items.summary: Carlos Yulo will return to OAJLP Gymnastique for another season after helping the club win France’s Top 12 men’s championship in May. The Filipino Olympic champion is preparing for the 2027 World Championships in Chengdu, an Olympic qualifying event for Los Angeles 2028.

items.title: Naomi Cesar wins historic Youth Olympics 800m silver
items.summary: Naomi Cesar won silver in the women’s 800 metres at the Dakar Youth Olympic Games, finishing in 2:09.34. A late surge lifted her from fourth to second, securing the Philippines’ first athletics medal at the event and its second Youth Olympic medal overall.
items.image_alt: Naomi Cesar at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games

items.title: Madi Mojdeh targets seven events in NCAA swimming title defence
items.summary: La Salle Green Hills swimmer Madi Mojdeh is set to compete in seven individual events as NCAA Season 102 swimming opens on November 10 at Rizal Memorial Sports Complex. Last season’s Rookie of the Year will help LSGH defend its championship alongside teammate Yugo Cabana.

items.title: Abra beats San Juan to move one win from MPBL National Finals
items.summary: Abra Solid North defeated San Juan 76–65 to take a 2–0 lead in the MPBL North Division Finals. DJ Fenner scored 20 points and Dave Ildefonso added 16 points and 11 rebounds. The defending national champions need one more victory to advance.
items.image_alt: Abra’s Raven Gonzales in MPBL action against San Juan

items.title: Delos Reyes’s late layup lifts La Salle women past NU
items.summary: Eli Delos Reyes scored with 3.7 seconds left as La Salle edged NU 84–83, ending a seven-game losing streak in UAAP women’s basketball. Kyla Go led with 32 points, while Bukky Ojo added 24 points and 24 rebounds as La Salle improved to 2–8.
items.image_alt: La Salle’s Eli Delos Reyes in UAAP women’s basketball action against NU
items.image_credit: UAAP Season 89 Media Team / Tiebreaker Times

items.title: Ginebra and San Miguel contest final PBA semifinal berth
items.summary: Barangay Ginebra and San Miguel meet in a deciding Game 5 at 7:30 pm on November 10 at Ynares Center in Antipolo. San Miguel recovered from 0–2 down to level the quarterfinal series. The winner advances to face defending champion TNT.
items.image_alt: San Miguel’s George King and Ginebra’s Jordan Murphy in PBA action

items.title: PLDT and Farm Fresh face off for PVL semifinal boost
items.summary: PLDT and Farm Fresh meet at 1 pm on November 10 at Smart Araneta Coliseum, both carrying 3–2 records in the PVL Siklab Series. The winner takes solo third place as PLDT targets a fourth straight victory and both teams pursue semifinal berths.
items.image_alt: PLDT volleyball team celebrating during a PVL match
items.image_credit: Photograph courtesy of PVL / Daily Tribune

items.title: Boatwright expected to join Gilas in Malaysia on November 23
items.summary: Tim Cone expects Bennie Boatwright to join Gilas Pilipinas in Malaysia on November 23, after his release from China’s Fujian Sturgeons. The late arrival leaves limited preparation time for the November FIBA qualifiers, while Carl Tamayo will miss the window with an ankle injury.
items.image_alt: Bennie Boatwright

items.title: UAAP suspends Ateneo coach Louie Alas for two games
items.summary: The UAAP imposed a two-game suspension on Ateneo coach Louie Alas for accumulated infractions and unsportsmanlike conduct after the UP game. He will miss the Blue Eagles’ November 11 matchup with Adamson and November 15 meeting with UST.
items.image_alt: Ateneo head coach Louie Alas during UAAP Season 89

items.title: UST girls reach UAAP semifinals as NUNS earns twice-to-beat edge
items.summary: UST swept UPIS 25–14, 25–15, 25–14 to secure a UAAP Season 89 girls’ volleyball semifinal berth and improve to 9–2. NUNS defeated Ateneo in straight sets, extending its unbeaten record to 12 matches and claiming the first twice-to-beat advantage.
items.image_alt: UST team in the UAAP Season 89 girls’ volleyball tournament

items.title: UE and NUNS secure UAAP boys’ volleyball Final Four places
items.summary: UE beat Adamson in four sets and NUNS swept UPIS to complete the UAAP Season 89 boys’ volleyball Final Four. Steven David scored 29 points for UE, while NUNS earned its 14th consecutive semifinal appearance. UST and FEU-Diliman also secured twice-to-beat advantages.
items.image_alt: UE Junior Red Warriors in the UAAP Season 89 boys’ volleyball tournament

items.title: Alfonso Siklab wins MPPT Imus leg after ending Titans’ streak
items.summary: Alfonso Siklab beat Rizal Ilustrados 3–1 to claim the MPPT Invitational’s third-leg title in Imus, Cavite. They reached the final by defeating two-leg champions Parañaque Titans 3–2, securing a 25–18 tiebreaker victory before winning the championship’s two mixed doubles matches.
items.image_alt: Alfonso Siklab pickleball team
items.image_credit: Maharlika Pilipinas Pickleball Tour via Instagram / Pickleball News Asia

items.title: Olivarez beats Tangub to claim National Open tennis crown
items.summary: Eric Jed Olivarez defeated Eric Jay Tangub 6–3, 6–4 to win the men’s singles title at the Mayor Edwin Olivarez National Open Tennis Championships in Sucat. The 28-year-old earned ₱100,000, adding another championship to his record on the Philippine tennis circuit.
items.image_alt: Eric Jed Olivarez holding his trophy alongside Eric Jay Tangub and tournament officials

items.title: Pangasinan launches Governor’s Cup pickleball tournament
items.summary: More than 1,200 players joined the opening of Pangasinan’s first Governor’s Cup pickleball tournament at Alibaba Pickleball Courts in Villasis. The competition brings together 35 towns and 25 clubs, with singles, doubles and mixed doubles divisions covering children through players aged 60 and above.
items.image_alt: Opening of Pangasinan’s Governor’s Cup pickleball tournament in Villasis
items.image_credit: JP De Vera / PIMRO — Provincial Government of Pangasinan

items.title: Mangubat earns weekly award after powering JRU’s strong finish
items.summary: Lawrence Mangubat earned Collegiate Press Corps Player of the Week honours after helping JRU finish the NCAA group stage at 10–3. He scored 19 points against Mapua and a career-high 27 against Benilde as the Heavy Bombers secured a twice-to-beat quarterfinal advantage.
items.image_alt: JRU guard Lawrence Mangubat in NCAA Season 102

items.title: Bagay and Castillo power EAC to NCAA quarterfinal advantage
items.summary: Jude Bagay and EJ Castillo scored 23 points each as EAC defeated Arellano 102–93 in NCAA Season 102 men’s basketball. The Generals finished the group stage at 7–6, secured Group B’s second seed and earned a twice-to-beat advantage in the quarterfinals.
items.image_alt: EAC’s EJ Castillo playing against the Arellano Chiefs

items.title: Short-handed Mapua edges Lyceum ahead of NCAA play-in rematch
items.summary: Mapua held off Lyceum 71–68 despite missing three key players in NCAA Season 102 men’s basketball. Kyle Timbol scored 20 points and Russel Liwanag added 12 points and 10 rebounds. The teams meet again Thursday, with Mapua holding a twice-to-beat advantage.
items.image_alt: Mapua University’s Kyle Timbol in NCAA Season 102

items.title: Criss Cross sweeps AEP-Cabstars to stay unbeaten at 5–0
items.summary: Criss Cross defeated AEP-Cabstars 25–15, 25–12, 25–20 to secure a fifth straight Spikers’ Turf Invitational Conference victory. Francis Saura led with 13 points and Jude Garcia added 11 as the defending champions maintained their unbeaten record while resting several key players.
items.image_alt: Criss Cross player Francis Saura in Spikers’ Turf action
items.image_credit: Courtesy of Spikers’ Turf / Daily Tribune

items.title: Absin leads FEU-DN Steel past previously unbeaten ClearSkiiin
items.summary: Charles Absin scored 23 points as FEU-DN Steel defeated ClearSkiiin 27–29, 25–19, 25–22, 25–21 in the Spikers’ Turf Invitational Conference. The Tamaraws ended a two-game losing streak and handed the UV Smashers their first defeat after four consecutive wins.
items.image_alt: FEU’s Charles Absin attacks against ClearSkiiin in Spikers’ Turf

items.title: Alpha Insurance sweeps 3B for third straight Spikers’ Turf victory
items.summary: Alpha Insurance beat 3B 25–16, 25–20, 25–22 to earn its third consecutive Spikers’ Turf Invitational Conference win. The Protectors recorded 14 kill blocks, including six from Jetlee Gopio, while Reymark Betco led their scoring with 10 points.
items.image_alt: Alpha Insurance players celebrate a point against 3B

items.title: Savouge beats VNS-Laticrete for third straight Spikers’ Turf win
items.summary: Savouge defeated VNS-Laticrete 25–10, 25–13, 20–25, 25–19 for its third consecutive victory in the Spikers’ Turf Invitational Conference. Joeven Dela Vega led with 20 points, while Mark Calado added 17 as the Spin Doctors improved to a 3–2 record.
items.image_alt: Savouge’s Joeven Dela Vega in action against VNS-Laticrete

items.title: Adamson sweeps Benilde to secure SSL quarterfinal seed
items.summary: Adamson secured the No. 3 quarterfinal seed in the Shakey’s Super League Unity Cup with a 26–24, 25–15, 25–21 win over Benilde. Shaina Nitura returned after missing three games, helping the Lady Falcons finish the Round of 8 with a victory.
items.image_alt: Adamson volleyball player Shaina Nitura
items.image_credit: UAAP Media Bureau / The Philippine Star

items.title: Fatherhood gives Niño Alcantara fresh motivation for tennis
items.summary: Filipino tennis veteran Niño Alcantara says fatherhood has renewed his motivation to compete. In a Rappler feature, he reflects on his career and representing the Philippines, while taking a short family break before preparing for 25 to 30 tournament weeks in 2027.
items.image_alt: Filipino tennis veteran Niño Alcantara featured by Rappler

items.title: Batangas advances to UCAL volleyball Final Four
items.summary: Defending champion University of Batangas swept Centro Escolar University 25–17, 25–20, 25–23 to reach the UCAL Season 9 men’s volleyball semifinals. The Brahmans will face Immaculada Concepcion College on November 10, while PCU-Dasmariñas meets top-seeded Lyceum in the other semifinal.
items.image_alt: University of Batangas Brahmans playing against CEU in UCAL volleyball

items.title: UE ends 30-game UAAP losing streak with win over Adamson
items.summary: UE defeated Adamson 53–47 to end a 30-game UAAP men’s basketball losing streak and claim its first victory since October 2024. Tope Lagat and Mo Tanedo scored 14 points each, while JM Edoukou added 13 points and 10 rebounds.
items.image_alt: UE Red Warriors player Tope Lagat

items.title: UP beats Ateneo to clinch eighth straight UAAP Final Four berth
items.summary: UP earned an eighth consecutive UAAP men’s basketball Final Four berth by defeating Ateneo 82–74. Veejay Pre scored 16 points as the Fighting Maroons extended their winning streak to seven games and improved to 9–2. Ateneo slipped to 5–6.
items.image_alt: Elliot Dimaculangan of the UP Fighting Maroons in UAAP Season 89

items.title: Bacolod prepares for December Pickleball Invasion tournament
items.summary: Bacolod will host Pickleball Invasion 2026 from December 4 to 6, with Grace Pharmacy and UNILAB presenting the event. Organisers aim to bring players and sports communities together, while venue details, competition categories and registration guidelines will be announced through official channels.

items.title: Cebu’s Juvey Veloso earns ICA pickleball coach educator certification
items.summary: Juvey Veloso has become one of three ICA-certified pickleball coach educators in the Philippines. Based in Cebu, he can train and assess aspiring coaches locally, reducing the need to travel elsewhere for certification. His first Cebu City course is scheduled for November 28.
items.image_alt: Juvey Veloso with fellow pickleball coaches and educators

items.title: Nxled sweeps Capital1 to stay unbeaten in PVL
items.summary: Nxled defeated Capital1 in straight sets, 25–13, 25–20, 25–18, to improve to 5–0 in the PVL All-Filipino Conference Siklab Series. Brooke Van Sickle led with 13 points, while MJ Phillips added nine as the Chameleons claimed the outright lead.
items.image_alt: Nxled Chameleons in the PVL All-Filipino Conference Siklab Series

items.title: Unbeaten UST women book UAAP Final Four place
items.summary: UST’s Growling Tigresses secured a UAAP Season 89 Final Four berth with a 95–48 win over FEU. Oma Onianwa scored 25 points as the defending champions remained unbeaten at 10–0, while Karylle Sierba added 13 points.
items.image_alt: UST Growling Tigresses in their UAAP women’s basketball game against FEU

items.title: Taduran keeps IBF crown with unanimous win over Moreno
items.summary: Pedro Taduran retained his IBF minimumweight championship with a unanimous-decision victory over Spain’s Brandon Moreno in Albuquerque. The Filipino boxer completed his fourth consecutive successful title defence, improving to 21–4–1 while handing Moreno the first defeat of his professional career.
items.image_alt: Pedro Taduran featured in GMA News’ report on his IBF title defence

items.title: Soyud and Lacsina power Akari past Choco Mucho in five sets
items.summary: Akari survived a five-set battle against Choco Mucho to level its PVL Siklab Series record at 3–3. Eli Soyud and Ivy Lacsina each scored 17 points, with Lacsina also contributing 11 digs and 14 excellent receptions.
items.image_alt: Eli Soyud of Akari playing against Choco Mucho in the PVL Siklab Series

items.title: Acido leads UST to one-point win over FEU
items.summary: UST halted a three-game losing run with an 86–85 victory over FEU in UAAP Season 89. Amiel Acido led the Growling Tigers with 23 points, helping improve their record to 5–6 as FEU slipped to 6–5.
items.image_alt: Amiel Acido of the UST Growling Tigers in UAAP Season 89

items.title: Deloria earns weekly PVL award after Galeries Tower breakthrough
items.summary: Erika Deloria earned PVL Press Corps Player of the Week honours for November 3–7 after helping Galeries Tower secure its first Siklab Series victory. She scored 20 points and delivered 28 excellent receptions in the five-set win over Akari.
items.image_alt: Erika Deloria of Galeries Tower in the PVL All-Filipino Conference

items.title: Eala closes milestone season with Hong Kong runner-up finish
items.summary: Alex Eala finished her 2026 season as Hong Kong Open runner-up. Her year included a maiden WTA singles title in Washington, a Birmingham WTA 125 crown, and appearances in Wimbledon’s last 16 and the US Open’s last 32.
items.image_alt: Alex Eala featured in GMA News’ 2026 season recap
items.image_credit: LTA/Instagram; Mubadala DC Open/Facebook; Matthew Stockman/Getty Images North America/Getty Images via AFP / GMA News Online

items.title: Quezon Memorial Circle opens free pickleball courts
items.summary: Two pickleball courts have opened at Quezon Memorial Circle, offering free play for Quezon City residents, with non-residents also welcome. Players can request a slot by email and should bring their own paddle, ball and reusable water bottle.
items.image_alt: Pickleball courts at Quezon Memorial Circle

items.title: NU edges La Salle to strengthen UAAP Final Four bid
items.summary: National University beat La Salle 84–80 in UAAP Season 89. Reinhard Jumamoy contributed 21 points, including 14 in the final quarter, as NU improved its record to eight wins and three losses.
items.image_alt: NU Bulldogs and DLSU Green Archers in UAAP Season 89
